- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) followed by true price drop, suppress next forecast peak by 10–15% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.1) and model forecasts high volatility, reduce forecast mean by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- When true price deviates >3% from forecast in first 3–5 days, adjust next 7-day forecast downward by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of true price, but don’t overcorrect.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overpredicts by 2–4% in 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 5 days to align with sentiment-driven correction.
